title: My dad will pay cash for my house. Should I still take a loan?
videoTitle: ASKING SEAN #232 | TO PAY FULL CASH OR TAKE LOAN?
excerpt: A young professional in Singapore can buy a house of just under RM1 million in cash with his father's help. Sean explains why he would still borrow, and three ways to use the money.

qa.asker: Low, a viewer who wrote in by email
qa.context: Low works in Singapore. His father has offered to pay cash, just under RM1 million, for a property, or alternatively to help with the down payment while Low pays the instalments himself. Low plans to rent it out for a few years and live in it when he moves back to Malaysia.
qa.question: Should he buy the property outright with his father's cash, or take a housing loan?
qa.quote: I will go for loan because it gives me more flexibility.
qa.answer: Take a loan. Either park the cash in a full flexi loan to cut the interest while keeping it withdrawable, use it to buy two or three high-yield subsale investments, or keep it invested elsewhere while the rent pays the loan. Paying fully in cash ties everything up in one illiquid asset.

reasons.title: Property is hard to turn back into cash
reasons.body: A purchase takes six to eight months to complete, selling quickly means selling below market, you can't refinance without built-up equity, and unlike shares you can't sell part of it in an emergency.

reasons.title: A flexi loan saves interest and stays liquid
reasons.body: Interest is calculated daily on what you owe, and in the early years about 88% to 90% of each instalment is interest. Parking the cash in a full flexi account cuts that sharply, and you can still withdraw it.

reasons.title: Capital opens the subsale market
reasons.body: Few young buyers can pay about 18% upfront, about RM144,000 on an RM800,000 subsale plus RM50,000 to RM80,000 for renovation. With it, you can see the unit, its rent and neighbours' prices first, and buy only at 5.5% to 6% yield or better.

reasons.title: Interest is less scary than it looks
reasons.body: A RM500,000 loan over 35 years costs about RM429,000 in interest, but property has risen about 4.3% to 4.5% a year over the past decade, and inflation shrinks the real value of that interest over time.

actions: Buy with a housing loan and place the cash in a full flexi account to reduce interest.
Or, use the capital for one subsale at a time: buy, furnish, rent out, then use six months of rent records for the next loan.
Set a minimum yield, such as 5.5% to 6% of the price, before buying any investment unit.
Buy for a clear purpose, investment or own stay, not a 'just in case' home for when you return.
Ask your father what he intends the money for, and show him a plan for how you would use it.
qa.caveat: If your father's wish is simply to give you a fully paid home, and the sum is a small part of his wealth, buying in cash is not wrong. Sean also warns against putting family money into friends' business ventures you don't understand.

sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #232. The quoted answer is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as Sean stated them in November 2023; loan rates and price growth change.
